proposed.sourceName: SeekersGuidance (Hanafi) — 'Is Rennet in Cheese Halal or Haram to Consume?' (Mawlana Ilyas Patel, checked by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani)
proposed.paraphrase: Even on the permissive Hanafi view that non-porcine rennet is lawful, the answer still advises avoiding when the source is unknown and stresses that porcine-derived rennet is prohibited — so a lenient consumer cannot simply presume unknown-source whey halal, because the source could be porcine.

proposed.sourceName: Darul Iftaa New York — 'Hanafi Ruling on Rennet from Non-Pork Animals not Zabiha' (Mufti Muajul I. Chowdhury)
proposed.paraphrase: The fatwa holds that even under the lenient Hanafi principle that non-pork rennet is pure, conventional extraction contaminates the product with impure stomach tissue, so most contemporary animal rennet is najis; only microbial or properly-slaughtered rennet is clearly lawful — leaving unknown-source whey doubtful rather than presumptively permissible.

researcherNote: whey seeded lenient = grade 3 (Questionable — contested), NOT grade 2. The lenient (Hanafi-permit) position still does not reach 'widely accepted' for UNKNOWN-source whey, because (a) the source could be porcine pepsin (haram in all schools) and (b) the modern extraction-contamination caveat. Both tier-1 sources support 'avoid/doubtful when source unknown.' Two independent sources. INTEGRITY: did not stretch lenient to halal. APPROVED by owner 2026-07-01.
